prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: システム連携用語表 (language ja).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "用語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 210px
  col 2: header "英語" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 163px
  col 3: header "説明" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 860px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A Japanese-language glossary for systems integration: each row pairs a Japanese term with its English equivalent and a short explanatory definition, so readers can identify a concept and then understand it.","reading":"Readers scan the first column for the Japanese term, glance across to the English label for recognition, then read the description for meaning. The first two columns act as a paired index; the third is explanatory prose.","groups":["Columns 1 and 2 belong together as the term/English label pair identifying the same concept.","Column 3 stands apart as the explanatory text and can absorb most wrapping."],"keep_intact":["Japanese technical terms in column 1 where possible, especially compound terms that are hard to reparse after wrapping.","English single-word identifiers in column 2; the longest unbreakable token needs about 103px of text width.","Header labels and the row-identifying first-column values."],"may_wrap":["Description text in column 3, which is long prose and can naturally occupy multiple lines.","Multiword English phrases such as “service level agreement” at spaces.","Longer Japanese terms in column 1 if that column is deliberately narrowed."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [232, 140, 347] · table 720×547px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 83, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [236, 152, 331] · table 720×593px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [231, 126, 362] · table 720×524px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
